Chicken shishlik (very tender + my fave)

Shawarma-spiced cauliflower

⭐️ 100/10 — Finally made it to Laser Wolf and I was very impressed! The views, the food, the prices, and the COCKTAILS were all impeccable! 😍 Located on the rooftop of the Hoxton Hotel is Laser Wolf — a tapas / prefixe style Israeli restaurant with some of the best sharing dishes in this world! 🌏 While waiting for my seat to be ready, I waited at the bar downstairs and ordered an espresso martini. ☕️ While the espresso martini was fine, it wasn’t anything extraordinary or out of this world. It was just all right! ☺️ I carried it upstairs and finished it shortly after sitting down, and then ordered No Big Dill. This was exactly as it is described — a gin martini with a very dill taste to it. Absolutely LOVED this one — it almost had a hint of spice to it?! 😍 anyways, it went down quickly. 🥒 Finally, I tried their house Gibson called Aunt Debbie. 🧅 this was such a good Gibson martini ! 😇 not the best I have had but definitely up there. Strong too! 🤣 I loved the Salatim appetizer with all of the different veggies & dips. It was unlimited refills too so you know I got a bunch more pita breads and hummus. 🫓 for my main I got the eggplant. 🍆 this dish literally tasted chewy like meat, despite being vegetarian?! 🌱 and then the oat milk soft serve was actually some of the best ice cream I have had in my lifeeee. 🍨 Definitely will be back here! As we continue to grow and plan thoughtfully for the future of our team, we’d like to share an important update with our guests.

We’re incredibly grateful for the love, support, and sweet moments you’ve shared with us. 

And for now, you have five more days to get your hands on your favorite treats!

Thank you for being part of our journey ❤️

Since West village is full of aesthetic cafes, I tried to visit as much as possible during my short period of time in NYC. I went to this retro Japanese bakery right at their opening cuz we have a full schedule that day. They specialized in gluten free Japanese sandos and pastries. They have such a cute interior with fun colours. I really wanted to get the fruit sandos but it was so early in the morning, I wanted something savory instead. I got a half portion of the egg sando and half portion of the chicken katsu sando. Both of them actually tasted really good, I really enjoyed how flavorful everything was. My only complaint would be the bread itself. Since it is gluten free, the texture is much softer than a regular piece of bread. It almost feels like a cake and it soak up the sauce very fast so it became a bit soggy. Still overall I do it’s a pretty nice place to chill. If you are in the area I would recommend coming for a drink or a little snack✨

In 2022, I was lucky enough to be hired as the social media manager at @murrayscheese, an iconic New York City cheese shop and national brand. It was the moment I really felt like I’d found my place in the food and beverage world. Cheese boards were already part of my life as I was making them for friends’ parties and my own hosting adventures, so getting a job where I was creating content around them felt like an actual dream.

My three years at Murray’s taught me so much and gave me countless opportunities. And honestly, it was just so much fun. I tasted hundreds of cheeses, researched products and makers to create accurate and thoughtful content, filmed at our shops with mongers, in restaurants with chefs, inside our cheese caves with affineurs, during weekly classes with instructors, and I even traveled to Wisconsin to capture creameries in action. I partnered with brands and stayed connected with local and national influencers. I’m so grateful for everything I learned and everyone I got to learn from.

Last March, I made the decision to leave Murray’s, and finally did something I’d been dreaming about for a long time…

We thought we knew cheese… and then NYC humbled us. 😅🧀

Here are 3 things that truly surprised us at Cheese Bootcamp:

1️⃣ Milk composition changes daily.
We learned that the fat, protein, and moisture levels in milk shift depending on the animal’s diet, season, and even time of day - and cheesemakers adjust their techniques every single batch to keep the final cheese consistent. 🤯

2️⃣ Affinage is 90% environment, 10% cheese.
The cave’s humidity, airflow, microbes, and even how often a wheel is flipped can completely transform its flavour and texture. It’s basically cheese + climate = magic. ✨

3️⃣ Sensory evaluation is a trained skill - not just “tasting.” We learned how professionals break down cheese using structured techniques: aroma families, texture analysis, flavour development, and even how different parts of the paste taste differently. It’s way more scientific (and fun!) than we ever imagined.

NYC definitely expanded our love for the craft - and we can’t wait to bring this knowledge back to the Prairies.

When Quicke’s cuts exact weight portions of their prestigious mature cheddar, a core cylinder gets removed. These mini truckles find their way to Murray’s Cheese Caves in NYC, where our team coats them in spices. The result? A marriage of heritage cheddar and uniquely bold flavors. 
 
Black Lime brings bright tropical citrus notes that match the cheese’s natural acidity. Roasted Curry adds a little heat and brings out the savory, earthy aromas in the cheese. Both have that classic cheddar crumble you love, with bold spices leading the way.

craft wheels rooted in cheesemaking tradition using high-quality milk from nearby small

flushing chinatown, queens 🥟

they say every chinatown tells a story - of migration, memory, and home. i’ve visited many across the country, but flushing felt different: it’s one of the few that truly feels like stepping into asia.
flushing’s chinatown began in the 1970s, when chinese and taiwanese immigrants moved here from manhattan’s overcrowded chinatown. over time, it’s grown into one of the largest and most diverse asian enclaves in the u.s., home to immigrants from mainland china, taiwan, hong kong, korea, and beyond.
walking through downtown flushing felt like being back in taipei or hong kong…the chatter spilling from restaurants, the smell of fresh buns, the hum of traffic and energy all around. it’s vibrant, unapologetic, and alive.
this visit was extra special! it marks my 25th chinatown for my 25th birthday 🥹💛 what started as a personal project to visit every chinatown in the u.s. has become a journey of learning, healing, and belonging.
flushing reminded me that chinatowns aren’t relics of the past - they’re living, breathing reflections of who we are and who we continue to become. 🌸

We had an absolute feast at @christossteakhouse. The menu is substantial, and there were many items that looked good but we didn’t order, so those will have to be for another time.

Bread and tapenade were brought to the table and it was a nice way to start the meal. The tapenade was quite tasty! We ordered a Mojito, which tasted great and was refreshing. For a starter, we had the Saganaki (pan-fried Viahotyni cheese), and that was fun. We really enjoyed the melted and gooey cheese. For sides we had the Brussels sprouts (very good, and it was nice that raisins were in the dish), and creamy classic mashed potatoes, which were really creamy and delicious. LIC’s taco brunch spot you need to know 🌮✨
Citrico Cafe serves up a fun AYCE (all-you-can-eat) weekend brunch with three options: tacos only ($20), drinks only ($25), or both ($40). We went with the taco AYCE and were surprised that every taco was delicious—even the vegetarian one had amazing flavor balance.

Each order comes with two tacos, and there are five flavors to choose from (plus a beef option outside the AYCE). We also added Chips & Guacamole ($13) and Corn Ribs ($11) from the a la carte menu—both solid picks.

The vibe is relaxed and lively, perfect for a group brunch. While we only ate enough to break even, big eaters and taco lovers will be in heaven here. Bonus: a photographer was snapping group shots for the restaurant collab ($20/print)—our group photo turned out surprisingly great 🤣

Definitely a fun, casual spot for tacos + friends in LIC 😋
